question_text: According to the course material, Halogen Security Company Limited was incorporated in July 1992 and granted a licence to operate in November of the same year, in response to a gap in:
option_a: The quality of guard service delivery in Nigeria
option_b: The supply of imported security equipment
option_c: The number of registered lawyers in Nigeria
option_d: The availability of foreign currency in Nigeria
explanation: Halogen Security Company Limited was incorporated in July 1992 as a Private Limited Liability Company and granted a licence in November of the same year, as a reaction to a gap in the quality of guard service delivery in Nigeria.

question_text: According to the course material, Halogen Security belongs to several professional associations, including the Institute of Industrial Security and Safety of Nigeria and:
option_a: The Association of Private Security Practitioners of Nigeria (APSPN)
option_d: The Nigerian Union of Journalists exclusively
explanation: Halogen Security belongs to several professional associations, including the Institute of Industrial Security and Safety of Nigeria, the Nigerian Institute of Safety Professionals, and the Association of Private Security Practitioners of Nigeria (APSPN).

question_text: According to the course material, Katz identifies three sources of conflict in an organisation such as a Private Security Company: structural conflict, role conflict, and:
option_a: Resources conflict
option_d: Religious conflict exclusively
explanation: Katz identifies three sources of organisational conflict: structural conflict (arising from interdependence between sub-units), role conflict (arising from prescribed behaviour), and resources conflict (competition over organisational resources).

question_text: According to the course material, Robbins identifies three sources of organisational conflict as communicational, structural, and:
option_a: Personal, stemming from individual differences
option_b: International, stemming from foreign policy disputes
option_d: Financial, stemming exclusively from currency exchange rates
explanation: Robbins identifies three sources of organisational conflict: communicational (misunderstandings), structural (organisational roles), and personal (stemming from individual differences).

question_text: According to the course material, the three types of conflict discussed in relation to Private Security Companies are intrapersonal, interpersonal, and:
option_a: Interdepartmental
option_d: Interspecies
explanation: The three types of conflict discussed are intrapersonal (internal to the individual), interpersonal (between individuals in a dyadic relationship), and interdepartmental (structural conflict between departments with scarce resources).

question_text: According to the course material, three main existing options for regulating the private security sector are banning illegal activities, licensing of individual firms, and:
option_a: Self-regulation through self-imposed codes of conduct
option_b: Complete nationalization of all private security companies
option_c: Total deregulation with no oversight whatsoever
option_d: Exclusive regulation by foreign governments
explanation: Three main existing options for regulation are banning activities deemed illegal, licensing of individual firms (and sometimes approving particular contracts), and self-regulation through self-imposed codes of conduct and standards.

question_text: According to the course material, at least five separate private security associations exist in Nigeria, with the oldest being the Nigerian Chapter of the:
option_a: American Society for Industrial Security (ASIS)
option_c: International Committee of the Red Cross
option_d: World Trade Organization
explanation: The oldest of Nigeria's private security associations is the Nigerian Chapter of the American Society for Industrial Security (ASIS), a global organisation supporting private industry standards, training and education.

question_text: According to the course material, the Association of Private Security Practitioners in Nigeria (APSPN) was founded in April 2004 in direct response to:
option_a: The government's decision to increase licence fees for guarding companies
option_d: The establishment of the NSCDC in 1967
explanation: APSPN was founded in April 2004 in direct response to the government's decision to increase licence fees for guarding companies, while the three other national associations were founded in 2002 in response to the arrival of Gray Security.

question_text: According to the course material, licences for private security companies in Nigeria have to be renewed by written application to the Ministry of Internal Affairs how often?
option_a: Every second year
option_d: Only once, permanently, at the time of first registration
explanation: Licences have to be renewed by written application to the Ministry of Internal Affairs every second year, though the course material notes there is otherwise little regulation or oversight of quality of service, standards, and training.

question_text: According to Sutherland (1939), cited in the course material, who first coined the term "white-collar crime", it is defined as an offence committed by:
option_a: A person of respectability and high social status in the course of his or her occupation
option_b: Only individuals who have never been formally employed
option_c: Exclusively foreign nationals operating illegally in Nigeria
option_d: Anyone under the age of eighteen
explanation: Sutherland (1939) first coined the term "white-collar crime", defining it as an offence committed by a person of respectability and high social status in the course of his or her occupation.

question_text: According to the course material, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was set up by the Nigerian federal government to curb the menace of:
option_a: Corruption and financial crime
option_d: Copyright disputes between musicians
explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was set up by the federal government to curb the menace of corruption and financial crime, given the overlap between white-collar crime and corporate crime.

question_text: According to the course material, one recommended method of "target hardening" as a defence against burglary involves applying basic security precautions to a facility, including attention to door construction, locks, alarms, and:
option_a: Surveillance devices
option_b: The colour of the building's exterior paint
option_d: The company's advertising budget
explanation: Target hardening means applying basic security precautions including attention to door construction, locks, alarms, and surveillance devices to reduce a facility's vulnerability to burglary.

question_text: According to the course material, the elements of the crime of robbery include trespass, taking, carrying away of personal property of another, intent to steal, and:
option_a: Accomplishing this from the person or presence of the victim by force or threat
option_b: The complete absence of any witnesses to the crime
option_c: A prior written agreement between the offender and the victim
option_d: The exclusive use of a firearm, with no other weapon qualifying
explanation: The elements of robbery are trespass, taking, carrying away of the personal property of another, with intent to steal, from the person or presence of the victim, by force or threat.

question_text: According to the course material, in the event of a labour dispute, security personnel's role is limited strictly to protecting personnel and property, and they are specifically instructed NOT to:
option_a: Photograph, tape, or report on the conduct of striking workers, beyond injury to personnel or property
option_b: Secure doors and gates not being used during the strike
option_c: Recover keys from employees going out on strike
option_d: Test fire and intrusion alarm systems after workers walk out
explanation: Security guards are specifically instructed not to photograph, tape, or report on the conduct of strikers; reports should relate only to injury to personnel or property, since their role is to protect, not to participate in the dispute.

question_text: According to the course material, industrial espionage commonly occurs in two ways: a dissatisfied employee appropriating information to advance their own interests, or:
option_a: A competitor seeking information to advance its own technological or financial interest
option_b: A government agency conducting a routine tax audit
option_c: A customer requesting a product refund
option_d: A shareholder attending an annual general meeting
explanation: Industrial espionage commonly occurs when a dissatisfied employee appropriates information to advance their own interests or damage the company, or when a competitor seeks information to advance its own technological or financial interest.

question_text: According to the course material, the well-known industrial espionage case between General Motors' German division Opel and Volkswagen, settled in 1997, resulted in Volkswagen agreeing to pay General Motors how much?
option_a: $100 million
option_d: $1 trillion
explanation: The Opel-Volkswagen industrial espionage case, following the move of Opel's production chief Jose Ignacio Lopez to Volkswagen, was settled in 1997 with Volkswagen agreeing to pay General Motors $100 million and to purchase at least $1 billion in car parts over 7 years.

question_text: According to the course material, piracy, defined as the illegal duplication and distribution of recordings, takes three specific forms: counterfeiting, bootlegging, and:
option_a: Pirating, the unauthorized duplication of sounds or images from a legitimate recording
option_b: Marketing, the legal promotion of an authentic product
option_c: Licensing, the legal granting of distribution rights
option_d: Franchising, the legal replication of a business model
explanation: Piracy takes three forms: counterfeiting (unauthorized recording plus duplication of artwork/trademark/packaging), pirating (unauthorized duplication of sounds or images from a legitimate recording), and bootlegging (unauthorized recording of a live broadcast or concert).

question_text: According to the Nigeria Copyright Commission (2007), cited in the course material, the Nigerian film industry loses an estimated amount annually to illegal digital duplication, online piracy, and unauthorized rental of video works. That amount is approximately:
option_a: N4.2 billion
explanation: According to the Nigeria Copyright Commission (2007), the film industry loses an estimated N4.2 billion annually to illegal digital duplication, online piracy, and unauthorized rental of video works within Nigeria.

question_text: According to the course material, the cartel of pirates involved in the piracy trade in Nigeria is domiciled in major markets, including Alaba International Market in Lagos and:
option_a: Main Market, Onitsha, in Anambra State
option_b: Only markets located outside of Nigeria
option_c: Exclusively online marketplaces with no physical presence
option_d: Only markets located in Abuja
explanation: The cartel of pirates is domiciled in big markets such as Alaba International Market in Lagos, Main Market in Onitsha, Anambra State, and other markets in Kano and Borno.

question_text: According to the course material, private security company conflict is described using a "three-dimensional conception" that considers the situation of incompatible goals, the structure of interaction, and:
option_a: The nature of their goals with other security operatives
option_b: The exact number of employees in each department
option_c: The physical size of the company's office building
option_d: The colour of the company's official uniform
explanation: The three-dimensional conception of conflict emphasizes the need to consider the situation of incompatible goals, the structure of interaction, and the nature of the parties' goals in relation to other security operatives.
